gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the DJI Power 1000 V2 takes solar panels only through DJI's separately sold Solar Panel Adapter Module (MPPT) or 1.8kW Solar/Car Super Fast Charger, so its sub-$400 price does not include a way to plug in a panel.
standout_why: Compared against PopSci's Black Friday deals page (the one cited), OutletPicks' 1,000–1,299Wh page, Backup Power Hub's deals page, Solar Generator Prices and JuiceBench. None gives a solar connector, voltage or adapter requirement for any 1 kWh unit. PopSci's only compatibility lines are that the Anker BP1000 fits the original C1000 only (not the Gen 2) and that BLUETTI Charger 1 pulls up to 560 W, without naming the stations it fits. OutletPicks and Backup Power Hub list the DJI at $379.99 with no mention of the adapter. It is not a 3 because the question does not ask about solar, and I could not open the maker pages for ChatGPT's own pick (Pecron E1000LFP) or for the ALLPOWERS P1800, so the cross-model comparison is incomplete.
decides: It confirms the DJI Power 1000 V2 as the pick for wall-charged outage backup, but only with a stated condition: a buyer who wants solar or alternator charging must add a DJI accessory (The Solar Lab puts the solar/car adapter at about $329), which takes the DJI well past $400. For that buyer the pick shifts to a unit with its own solar input: the BLUETTI Elite 100 mini (up to 350 W solar per BLUETTI, 700 W AC only) for light loads, or the ALLPOWERS P1800 / Pecron E1000LFP for 1,800 W loads, once their solar input specs are read from the maker pages I could not open. The DJI is also the only candidate with a maker-documented expansion path (up to five 2,048 Wh batteries).

findings.label: Solar input route
findings.value: Via the DJI Power Solar Panel Adapter Module (MPPT), one to three panels; or via the 1.8kW Solar/Car Super Fast Charger's XT90 port
findings.source_title: New DJI Power 1000 V2 Increases Stable Power Output for a Smarter, More Efficient Experience (DJI Europe press release, 9 July 2025)
findings.note: DJI's wording: "Connect to solar panels through the DJI Power Solar Panel Adapter Module (MPPT)" and "Connect to one to three solar panels". This is DJI's European press release, not the US product page; dji.com/power-1000-v2 and its specs page redirected to a 404 for my fetches. Quotes came through a page-summarising fetch, so check the wording against the page before printing.

findings.label: Accessories in the box
findings.value: None of the named accessories: "All named accessories are sold separately" (Expansion Battery 2000, 1kW and 1.8kW Super Fast Chargers, solar panels, Solar Panel Adapter Module (MPPT), storage case)
findings.source_title: New DJI Power 1000 V2 Increases Stable Power Output for a Smarter, More Efficient Experience (DJI Europe press release, 9 July 2025)
findings.note: SDC drone fast-charge cables are also sold separately per the same release.

findings.label: Solar and car input with the 1.8kW Solar/Car Super Fast Charger
findings.value: Up to 1,200 W solar plus 600 W continuous car power (DJI); the release's headline figure is up to 1,800 W solar input, footnoted
findings.source_title: New DJI Power 1000 V2 Increases Stable Power Output for a Smarter, More Efficient Experience (DJI Europe press release, 9 July 2025)
findings.note: DJI's two figures (1,200 W and 1,800 W solar) sit in the same release and I could not read the footnote that reconciles them. The 1kW Super Fast Car Charger recharges at up to 1,000 W from the alternator (DJI).

findings.label: Solar adapter: reviewer's cost and limit
findings.value: About $329 for DJI's solar and car charging adapter; The Solar Lab says the 1.8kW adapter "only allows you to hit a solar input rate of 600W" on this unit, with the other 600 W through a 12V-style input
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 Review: A Quieter, Faster Upgrade? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab's 600 W solar figure conflicts with DJI's 1,200 W; show both with names. The page shows no publication date or author name (copyright 2026). The Solar Lab describes the two SDC ports as proprietary and reports no measured solar wattage. Arithmetic: a $379.99 station (rival-page price, see below) plus about $329 is about $709.

findings.label: Expansion battery
findings.value: DJI Power Expansion Battery 2000 (2,048 Wh), up to five, 11,264 Wh total, connected by the designated cable
findings.source_title: New DJI Power 1000 V2 Increases Stable Power Output for a Smarter, More Efficient Experience (DJI Europe press release, 9 July 2025)
findings.note: 1,024 + 5 × 2,048 = 11,264 Wh. The Solar Lab confirms the battery connects through an SDC port.

findings.label: Core specs per DJI
findings.value: 1,024 Wh; 2,600 W stable AC output; 14.2 kg (about 31.3 lb); UPS switchover within 0.01 s
findings.source_title: New DJI Power 1000 V2 Increases Stable Power Output for a Smarter, More Efficient Experience (DJI Europe press release, 9 July 2025)
findings.note: 14.2 kg × 2.2046 = 31.3 lb (my conversion; DJI gives kg). The figures are footnoted in the release.

findings.label: Reviewer measurements
findings.value: 82% efficiency; about 18 W idle consumption (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 V2 Review: A Quieter, Faster Upgrade? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab gives no usable-Wh figure; 82% of 1,024 Wh would be about 840 Wh (my arithmetic, not their measurement).
